city.Guatemala.description: Guatemala is a Central American country packed with volcanoes and ancient Maya temples. The stone pyramids of Tikal rise above the rainforest, and beautiful Lake Atitlan sits ringed by three towering volcanoes.
city.Guatemala.landmark: steep stone temple pyramids of Tikal poking above the misty jungle canopy at dawn
city.Guatemala.greeting: Most people speak Spanish — say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Guatemala.flag: a blue stripe, a white stripe, and a blue stripe, with a bright green bird in the middle
city.Guatemala.clue.0: planned a trip to a Central American country full of steaming volcanoes
city.Guatemala.clue.1: wanted to climb ancient stone pyramids poking up above the rainforest at Tikal
city.Guyana.description: This country on the northern coast of South America is almost entirely covered in rainforest, home to the thundering Kaieteur Falls — and, unusually for the continent, English-speaking and cricket-mad.
city.Guyana.landmark: towering single plunge of Kaieteur Falls into a rainforest gorge with rising mist
city.Guyana.greeting: A surprise — it's the only country in South America where English is the official language, so just say “Hello.”
city.Guyana.flag: green with a big golden arrow and a red triangle, the “Golden Arrowhead”
city.Guyana.clue.0: raved about one of the tallest single-drop waterfalls in the world, deep in the rainforest
city.Guyana.clue.1: couldn't stop talking about a South American country that's cricket-mad and feels a bit Caribbean
city.Haiti.description: Haiti shares the mountainous island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, and its name means "land of high mountains." It is famous for brightly painted "tap-tap" buses, colorful folk art, and a giant mountaintop fortress.
city.Haiti.landmark: massive stone Citadelle Laferrière fortress atop a green mountain peak
city.Haiti.greeting: People speak Haitian Creole — say hello with “Bonjou” (bohn-ZHOO).
city.Haiti.flag: a blue band above a red band with a little palm tree in the center
city.Haiti.clue.0: kept repeating that the country's name means "land of high mountains"
city.Haiti.clue.1: couldn't wait to ride the brightly painted "tap-tap" buses covered in colorful pictures
city.Honduras.description: Honduras is a mountainous Central American country that was once a famous "banana republic." It has ancient Maya ruins at Copan, and the island of Roatan sits on a huge coral reef in the Caribbean Sea.
city.Honduras.landmark: intricately carved Maya stone stelae and temples of Copán in the jungle
city.Honduras.greeting: Most people speak Spanish — say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Honduras.flag: a blue stripe, a white stripe, and a blue stripe with five little blue stars in the middle
city.Honduras.clue.0: kept talking about giant banana plantations in an old "banana republic"
city.Honduras.clue.1: planned to explore the Maya ruins of Copan, with a stone stairway carved full of picture-writing
city.Honduras.clue.2: packed a purse of leftover lempira, named after a brave Indigenous chief
city.Jamaica.description: This mountainous island in the Caribbean is the birthplace of reggae music and its most famous singer, home to record-breaking sprinters, and known for fiery jerk cooking and the terraced waterfalls of Dunn's River.
city.Jamaica.landmark: cascading terraces of Dunn's River Falls tumbling down toward a palm beach
city.Jamaica.greeting: The official language is English, but locals greet you in Patois with “Wah gwaan” (wah-GWAHN), meaning “what's going on?”
city.Jamaica.flag: traced a flag with a golden X splitting it into green and black triangles
city.Jamaica.clue.0: kept humming bouncy reggae tunes and talking about the island's most famous singer
